task.description: WF-03 Step 1b re-check, rework iteration 1: independently re-verify docs/migration/decisions/0018-branch-protection-posture.md's rework against the two BLOCKER findings from the prior FAIL (grep-completeness claim in Consequences; decision (d) reasoning).

result.summary:
Independently re-ran `grep -rniE --include="*.md" "hard gate|structurally impossible|Backend gate|Frontend gate" docs/` myself. The design's claimed nine-file 'beyond ISS-0441's own three affected_files' set is CORRECT and matches my independent grep exactly: AGENT_SYSTEM.md, WF-02_requirement_implementation.md, WF-01_requirement_development.md, HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, 0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md, docs/agents/protocols/GIT_SETUP.md, docs/anti-patterns.md, 0011-frontend-ownership.md, 0017-task-queue-selection-model.md -- no file is missing and none extra. Each file's substantive characterization (agent-workflow-sequencing gate / worktree-checkout limitation / historical incident narration / future S8 scope / task-queue-locking claim) is accurate on inspection -- none of the nine actually asserts a current claim about main's git-merge protection, so the 'no change needed' conclusion is right for all nine.

However, one of the nine files' hit is misquantified in a way that is itself a checkable, false claim of the same kind this whole rework exists to eliminate: the design states 'docs/anti-patterns.md (three hits)' and describes exactly three narrative items. My independent grep of the exact same command shows FIVE real line-matches in docs/anti-patterns.md: line 1578 ('first `Backend gate` run failed on it' -- PR #681/lint_handoffs incident), line 1611 ('instead make it structurally impossible' -- proposed future ORCH-side check), line 1689 ('failed CI's backend gate on the very first run' -- REQ-167/PR #688, a DIFFERENT incident from line 1578, not the same one restated), line 1910 ('CI's backend gate runs' -- ISS-0069-focused task, a third distinct backend-gate incident), and line 1920 ('past FIVE separate hard gates' -- the incident the design's third bullet item describes). The design's three-item narrative silently merges three textually distinct backend-gate incidents (1578, 1689, 1910) into its single first bullet ('a specific Backend gate run failing during an earlier mistake'), undercounting the real hit count from five to three. The substance of the conclusion (all are historical incident narration, none asserts a current main-protection claim) still holds for all five lines on inspection -- so this does not change what correction, if any, anti-patterns.md needs (none) -- but the design's own explicit parenthetical count is factually wrong, checkable in one command, and appears in the exact passage this rework iteration was dispatched specifically to make precise after the prior FAIL's 'confirmed as the complete set' false-completeness finding. A governance ADR whose corrected-for-precision passage still contains a wrong, verifiable count is not close enough under this gate's no-partial-credit rule -- the whole point of iteration 1 was to stop asserting checkable things that are not actually true of the real grep output.

Decision (d)'s rewritten reasoning independently verified as sound: it correctly acknowledges the real reconfigure-(PUT enforce_admins:false or delete protection)-merge-restore override path exists under enforce_admins:true (no longer the false 'no override path at all' claim), and its argument for enforce_admins:false + --admin being preferable is substantive rather than hand-waving: (1) atomicity -- one flagged merge command vs. a multi-step disable/merge/re-enable sequence where a crash between steps silently leaves main unprotected for every subsequent run until noticed, a real and specific failure mode for an unattended multi-host pipeline; (2) granularity -- flipping enforce_admins is a repo-wide, standing-until-reversed setting change used to express what is really a single per-merge judgement call, correctly distinguishing 'this check is attributable elsewhere' from 'no check should block anyone until further notice'; (3) audit visibility -- --admin is a queryable property of the merge itself via gh pr view --json mergedBy,mergeCommit, whereas a protection-toggle-and-restore leaves no equivalent record tying the toggle to the specific PR it was for. All three grounds are concrete and pipeline-specific, not generic. This check PASSES.

git diff (6bd8c0da..be93708c) confirmed confined to decision (d) and the Consequences section of 0018-branch-protection-posture.md (plus the step-01-code-designer.json handoff itself) -- no other passage, including decisions (a)/(b)/(c) and the Step 1-4 command sequences already passed in iteration 0, was touched. This check PASSES.

Only one of three dispatch items fails, but per this gate's no-partial-credit rule that is sufficient for FAIL.
